cause: California does not grow soybeans at a scale NASS surveys. The API returns 'bad request' because no matching records exist, not because the query is malformed.
impact: Zero SOYBEANS rows for CA in the dataset. This is correct — it means the crop is not grown here, not that data is missing.
resolution: No rows are created. Do NOT fill with zeros — absence of rows means the crop is not grown. If your analysis filters to CA soybeans, expect an empty result.

cause: NASS returned 2,067 historical sorghum records for Iowa, but all predate the year 2000. Iowa stopped growing sorghum at survey-reportable scale before our analysis window.
impact: Zero SORGHUM rows for IA in the dataset.
resolution: Same as CA soybeans: absence means not grown, not missing. The raw API data (pre-2000) is archived in data/raw/nass/ if you want to explore historical patterns.

issue: Planted acres use different NASS filters than yield/harvested
query: AREA PLANTED for CORN and SORGHUM (all states)
cause: NASS reports planted acres at the total commodity level, not split by utilization practice (grain vs silage). Sending util_practice_desc=GRAIN with a planted-acres query returns HTTP 400. Yield and harvested acres ARE split by utilization, so the same filter works for those.
impact: If you query NASS for planted acres of corn or sorghum, do NOT include util_practice_desc in your parameters. For yield and harvested acres, you MUST include it to avoid double-counting grain and silage rows.
resolution: The pipeline drops util_practice_desc from planted-acres requests. The dedup filter also exempts AREA PLANTED from the ALL UTILIZATION PRACTICES removal step.

issue: Suppressed yields appear as zero, not null
query: YIELD for counties with few farms
cause: When a county has too few farms to publish without disclosing an individual operation, NASS suppresses the value. In the raw API response this shows up as Value='(D)' or Value='0' rather than null. A zero yield is not a real observation — it is a suppression code.
impact: 74 yield rows had value <= 0 and were set to NaN. If you pull NASS data yourself, always check for and null out zero yields.
resolution: The pipeline converts non-numeric values and zeros to NaN via pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce') and an explicit <= 0 check. The yield_status field in the master dataset distinguishes 'suppressed' from 'not_reported'.

issue: Duplicate rows from ALL UTILIZATION PRACTICES / ALL CLASSES
query: CORN, SORGHUM, WHEAT yield and harvested acres
cause: NASS sometimes publishes the same county-year observation under both a specific category (e.g. util_practice_desc=GRAIN) and an aggregate (ALL UTILIZATION PRACTICES). Similarly, winter wheat appears under both class_desc=WINTER and ALL CLASSES. Querying by short_desc alone returns both, doubling your rows.
impact: Without dedup, every downstream analysis is inflated. The duplicates are silent — row counts look plausible and no error is raised.
resolution: Pin util_practice_desc=GRAIN for corn/sorghum and class_desc=WINTER for wheat in yield/harvested queries. The pipeline also has a safety-net dedup that drops ALL UTILIZATION PRACTICES and ALL CLASSES rows (except for AREA PLANTED, which is only reported under ALL).

cause: NASS uses county_code 998 to publish aggregated data for suppressed counties. These rows have county_name 'OTHER (COMBINED) COUNTIES' and contain totals for all suppressed counties in the state, producing conflicting values that create duplicates.
impact: 1,342 rows removed. If you do not filter these, you get duplicate (fips, year, crop, statistic) keys and your joins will fan out.
resolution: Filter out county_code == '998' before any analysis. These are not real counties.
